data.name: NinjaScriptIndicatorDescriptionADL
data.value: Video Tutorial: www.youtube.com/watch?v=xbjJRaL81qo&list=PL3-s3qsUnfLSgA63mRRrNJv3lX4flD1UH&index=19&pp=iAQB\n\nADL (Accumulation/Distribution Line) is a cumulative volume-based indicator that relates price movement within each bar to its volume. When price closes in the upper portion of its range, volume is added; when it closes in the lower portion, volume is subtracted. The resulting line is intended to reflect buying or selling pressure over time and is often compared to price movement to evaluate confirmation or divergence.

data.name: NinjaScriptIndicatorDescriptionADX
data.value: Video Tutorial: www.youtube.com/watch?v=WdM2JlFJx7Q&list=PL3-s3qsUnfLSgA63mRRrNJv3lX4flD1UH&index=17&pp=iAQB ADX (Average Directional Index) measures the strength of a trend without indicating its direction. Higher values reflect stronger directional movement, while lower values suggest weaker or range-bound conditions. ADX is derived from positive and negative directional movement components (+DI and -DI), which are used to assess directional bias while ADX reflects overall trend strength. When ADX rises above the lower reference line, it is commonly interpreted as indicating the development of a stronger trend environment. Movement above the upper reference line is often associated with very strong trend conditions.

data.name: NinjaScriptIndicatorDescriptionADXR
data.value: ADXR (Average Directional Movement Rating) builds on ADX (Average Directional Index) by smoothing it over time to provide a more stable view of overall trend strength. Higher values indicate a stronger trend environment, while lower values suggest weaker or consolidating conditions. Because it is smoothed, ADXR typically reacts more slowly than ADX and is often used to confirm whether trend strength is persisting.

data.name: NinjaScriptIndicatorDescriptionAPZ
data.value: Video Tutorial: www.youtube.com/watch?v=Mzep8oQDZyA&list=PL3-s3qsUnfLSgA63mRRrNJv3lX4flD1UH&index=9\n\nAPZ (Adaptive Price Zone) plots dynamic upper and lower bands around a moving average using market volatility. As volatility increases, the bands widen; as volatility contracts, they narrow. Price movement near or beyond the outer bands can indicate relatively extended conditions compared to recent price behavior. APZ is commonly used to visualize changing volatility and potential price expansion or contraction zones.

data.name: NinjaScriptIndicatorDescriptionAroon
data.value: Video Tutorial: www.youtube.com/watch?v=2XnAxkMpQHs&list=PL3-s3qsUnfLSgA63mRRrNJv3lX4flD1UH&index=17\n\nAroon consists of Aroon Up and Aroon Down, which measure the number of bars since the most recent high and low within the selected Period. Values near the upper range suggest recent highs or lows occurred more recently, while lower values indicate they occurred further back in time. The relationship between Aroon Up and Aroon Down is often used to assess emerging trends or weakening momentum.

data.name: NinjaScriptIndicatorDescriptionAroonOscillator
data.value: Aroon Oscillator is derived from the Aroon indicator and plots the difference between the two values. Positive readings indicate recent highs occurred more recently than lows, while negative readings indicate the opposite. The oscillator fluctuates around zero and is commonly used to assess shifts in trend strength and directional bias.

data.name: NinjaScriptIndicatorDescriptionATR
data.value: ATR (Average True Range) measures market volatility by calculating the average range between high and low prices, including gaps, over the selected Period. Higher ATR values indicate increased price movement, while lower values reflect quieter conditions. ATR does not indicate direction; it is commonly used to assess relative volatility and how price movement is expanding or contracting over time.

data.name: NinjaScriptIndicatorDescriptionBollinger
data.value: Video Tutorial: www.youtube.com/watch?v=7UwjifDcW28&list=PL3-s3qsUnfLSgA63mRRrNJv3lX4flD1UH&index=6\n\nBollinger (Bollinger Bands) plots a moving average with upper and lower bands offset by a multiple of standard deviation. The bands expand as volatility increases and contract as volatility decreases. Price interacting with the outer bands can indicate relatively high or low levels compared to recent activity. Bollinger Bands are often used to visualize volatility shifts and relative price extremes.

data.name: NinjaScriptIndicatorDescriptionBOP
data.value: BOP (Balance of Power) measures the relationship between buyers and sellers by comparing the distance between open and close relative to the bar's range. Values above zero indicate that buyers controlled more of the session's range, while values below zero indicate greater selling control. BOP is typically used to gauge shifts in short-term control between bulls and bears.

data.name: NinjaScriptIndicatorDescriptionBuySellPressure
data.value: Buy Sell Pressure plots separate Buy Pressure and Sell Pressure values for each bar, representing the estimated percentage of the bar's activity attributed to buy versus sell orders. The two plots together reflect how order flow was distributed within the bar, showing the relative balance between buying and selling pressure. When Buy Pressure exceeds Sell Pressure, buying activity dominated that bar; when Sell Pressure is greater, selling activity dominated.\n\nThis indicator relies on intrabar order flow data and will only display historically when Tick Replay is enabled; otherwise, it plots in real-time only.

data.name: NinjaScriptIndicatorDescriptionCCI
data.value: CCI (Commodity Channel Index) is a momentum oscillator that measures how far price has deviated from its average over the selected Period. Values above zero indicate price is trading above its average, while values below zero indicate it is below. More extreme readings reflect greater deviation from typical price levels. CCI is often used to identify relative strength, weakness, and potential shifts in momentum.

data.name: NinjaScriptIndicatorDescriptionChaikinMoneyFlow
data.value: CMF (Chaikin Money Flow) is a volume-weighted indicator that measures buying and selling pressure over the selected Period. It evaluates where price closes within its range and combines that with volume to produce a value that fluctuates above and below zero. Positive readings suggest sustained accumulation, while negative readings suggest distribution. CMF is commonly used to assess whether volume is confirming price movement.

data.name: NinjaScriptIndicatorDescriptionChaikinOscillator
data.value: Chaikin Oscillator is derived from the ADL (Accumulation/Distribution Line) and plots the difference between two moving averages of ADL. It highlights changes in momentum behind accumulation and distribution. Rising values indicate increasing buying pressure relative to selling pressure, while falling values indicate the opposite. It is often used to identify shifts in money flow momentum.

data.name: NinjaScriptIndicatorDescriptionChaikinVolatility
data.value: Chaikin Volatility measures the rate of change in the trading range (high minus low) over a specified period. Increasing values reflect expanding price ranges and rising volatility, while decreasing values indicate contracting ranges. This indicator focuses on volatility expansion and contraction rather than price direction.

data.name: NinjaScriptIndicatorDescriptionCMO
data.value: CMO (Chande Momentum Oscillator) is a momentum indicator that measures the difference between the sum of recent gains and losses over the selected Period. It fluctuates above and below zero, with positive values reflecting stronger upward momentum and negative values reflecting stronger downward momentum. Because it accounts for both gains and losses directly, CMO can respond quickly to shifts in price momentum.

data.name: NinjaScriptIndicatorDescriptionConstantLines
data.value: Constant Lines draws one or more user-defined horizontal reference lines on the chart. These lines remain fixed at the specified price levels and do not adjust automatically with market data. This indicator is typically used to mark key price levels, thresholds, or custom reference values.

data.name: NinjaScriptIndicatorDescriptionCurrentDayOHL
data.value: Video Tutorial: www.youtube.com/watch?v=C5_spt0Yvhs&list=PL3-s3qsUnfLSgA63mRRrNJv3lX4flD1UH&index=16\n\nCurrent Day OHL (Current Day Open/High/Low) plots the current session's Open, High, and Low levels directly on the chart. The High and Low update throughout the session as new extremes are made, while the Open remains fixed at the session start. This indicator provides a clear reference to the active session's price range.

data.name: NinjaScriptIndicatorDescriptionDEMA
data.value: DEMA (Double Exponential Moving Average) is a moving average designed to reduce lag compared to a traditional EMA (Exponential Moving Average). It applies a smoothing technique that responds more quickly to recent price changes while still filtering short-term noise. DEMA is often used to track trend direction with faster responsiveness than standard moving averages.

data.name: NinjaScriptIndicatorDescriptionDM
data.value: DM (Directional Movement) plots +DI (Positive Directional Indicator), -DI (Negative Directional Indicator), ADX (Average Directional Index) to evaluate directional movement and overall trend strength over the selected Period. The +DI line measures upward directional movement, while the -DI line measures downward directional movement. When +DI crosses above -DI, it indicates upward momentum has overtaken downward momentum and is commonly interpreted as a bullish directional signal. When -DI crosses above +DI, it indicates downward momentum has overtaken upward momentum and is commonly interpreted as a bearish directional signal. ADX reflects the strength of the prevailing trend, regardless of which direction is dominant.

data.name: NinjaScriptIndicatorDescriptionDMI
data.value: DMI (Directional Movement Index) calculates a normalized measure of directional movement based on +DM and -DM over the selected Period. Values above zero indicate stronger upward directional movement, while values below zero indicate stronger downward directional movement. The closer the value is to zero, the more balanced the up and down movement has been.

data.name: NinjaScriptIndicatorDescriptionDMIndex
data.value: DM Index (Dynamic Momentum Index) is a variable-period RSI (Relative Strength Index) that automatically adapts its effective RSI lookback based on recent volatility. In more volatile conditions it uses a shorter period (more responsive), and in quieter conditions it uses a longer period (smoother). It is interpreted similarly to RSI, with higher readings commonly associated with overbought conditions and lower readings with oversold conditions.

data.name: NinjaScriptIndicatorDescriptionDonchianChannel
data.value: Video Tutorial: www.youtube.com/watch?v=3EhlGcyT3QU&list=PL3-s3qsUnfLSgA63mRRrNJv3lX4flD1UH&index=21\n\nDonchian Channel plots upper and lower bands based on the highest high and lowest low over the selected Period. The channel expands and contracts as new highs and lows are established. It is commonly used to visualize breakout levels and the current price range relative to recent extremes.

data.name: NinjaScriptIndicatorDescriptionDoubleStochastics
data.value: Double Stochastics is a stochastic calculation to a stochastic value, creating a smoothed momentum oscillator. The indicator fluctuates within a bounded range and highlights shifts in short-term momentum relative to recent price action. It is often used to identify changes in momentum intensity and potential overextended conditions.

data.name: NinjaScriptIndicatorDescriptionEaseOfMovement
data.value: EMV (Ease of Movement) measures how easily price moves relative to volume. It compares the change in price to the amount of volume required to produce that movement. Positive values indicate price is advancing with relatively less resistance, while negative values indicate price is declining with relative ease. EMV is commonly used to evaluate the relationship between price movement and underlying participation.

data.name: NinjaScriptIndicatorDescriptionEMA
data.value: Video Tutorial: www.youtube.com/watch?v=pcraBHC70B8&list=PL3-s3qsUnfLSgA63mRRrNJv3lX4flD1UH&index=19\n\nEMA (Exponential Moving Average) is a moving average that places greater weight on recent prices, allowing it to respond more quickly to current market changes than a simple moving average. The slope and position of the EMA are often used to assess trend direction and short-term momentum.

data.name: NinjaScriptIndicatorDescriptionFisherTransform
data.value: Fisher Transform applies a mathematical transformation to price data to create a normalized oscillator designed to highlight extreme movements. The indicator oscillates around zero and emphasizes shifts in momentum. Rapid reversals or line crossovers are commonly observed for changes in price momentum.

data.name: NinjaScriptIndicatorDescriptionFOSC
data.value: FOSC (Forecast Oscillator) measures the percentage difference between the current price and a linear regression forecast over the selected Period. Positive values indicate price is trading above the projected regression value, while negative values indicate it is below. FOSC is used to evaluate how far price has deviated from its statistically projected path.

data.name: NinjaScriptIndicatorDescriptionHMA
data.value: HMA (Hull Moving Average) is a weighted moving average designed to reduce lag while maintaining smoothness. It uses a calculation that combines weighted averages and a square-root period adjustment to respond quickly to price changes. HMA is commonly used to assess trend direction with reduced delay compared to traditional moving averages.

data.name: NinjaScriptIndicatorDescriptionIchimokuCloud
data.value: Ichimoku Cloud plots multiple components — Conversion (Tenkan), Base (Kijun), Leading (Senkou) Span A, Leading (Senkou) Span B, and Lagging (Chikou) — to provide a structured view of trend, momentum, and projected support/resistance. The area between Span A and Span B forms the "Cloud," which shifts forward in time. Relative positioning of price and the Cloud is commonly used to assess overall market structure.

data.name: NinjaScriptIndicatorDescriptionKAMA
data.value: KAMA (Kaufman's Adaptive Moving Average) is a moving average that adjusts its smoothing factor based on market efficiency. During trending conditions it becomes more responsive, and during sideways conditions it becomes smoother. KAMA is designed to reduce noise while adapting to changing price behavior.

data.name: NinjaScriptIndicatorDescriptionKeltnerChannel
data.value: Video Tutorial: www.youtube.com/watch?v=BRNYtRuy6QQ&list=PL3-s3qsUnfLSgA63mRRrNJv3lX4flD1UH&index=12\n\nKeltner Channel plots a moving average with upper and lower bands offset by a multiple of ATR (Average True Range). The bands expand and contract based on volatility. Price interaction with the outer bands is commonly observed to assess relative extension and volatility conditions.

data.name: NinjaScriptIndicatorDescriptionKeyReversalDown
data.value: Key Reversal Down evaluates each bar for a bearish key reversal condition, which occurs when the current bar makes a higher high than the prior bar and closes below the prior bar's close. When the condition is met, the indicator plots a value of 1 for that bar; otherwise, it plots 0. This output is designed for condition detection in analysis or strategy logic rather than visual pattern annotation.

data.name: NinjaScriptIndicatorDescriptionKeyReversalUp
data.value: Key Reversal Up evaluates each bar for a bullish key reversal condition, which occurs when the current bar makes a lower low than the prior bar and closes above the prior bar's close. When the condition is met, the indicator plots a value of 1 for that bar; otherwise, it plots 0. This output is intended for condition detection in analysis or strategy logic rather than visual pattern annotation.

data.name: NinjaScriptIndicatorDescriptionLinReg
data.value: Lin. Reg. (Linear Regression) plots the end-point value of a linear regression line calculated over the selected Period. The line represents the statistically best-fit trend of price for that lookback window and updates each bar. It is commonly used to visualize underlying trend direction and smoothing based on regression analysis.

data.name: NinjaScriptIndicatorDescriptionLinRegIntercept
data.value: Lin. Reg. Intercept (Linear Regression Intercept) plots the intercept value of the linear regression line over the selected Period. The intercept represents where the regression line would cross the price axis at the start of the lookback window. This indicator is primarily used for analytical or strategy development purposes related to regression calculations.

data.name: NinjaScriptIndicatorDescriptionLinRegSlope
data.value: Lin. Reg. Slope (Linear Regression Slope) measures the slope of the linear regression line over the selected Period. Positive values indicate an upward-sloping regression trend, while negative values indicate a downward slope. The magnitude reflects the strength of the directional bias within the regression window.

data.name: NinjaScriptIndicatorDescriptionMACD
data.value: Video Tutorial: www.youtube.com/watch?v=2CgisquYX7A&list=PL3-s3qsUnfLSgA63mRRrNJv3lX4flD1UH&index=22 MACD (Moving Average Convergence Divergence) plots the difference between a fast and slow EMA (Exponential Moving Average), along with a Signal line (an EMA of the MACD) and a histogram that represents the distance between the MACD and Signal lines. When the MACD value is above zero, the fast EMA is positioned above the slow EMA, indicating shorter-term momentum is stronger than the longer-term average. When below zero, the fast EMA is positioned below the slow EMA. Crossovers between the MACD and Signal lines, as well as changes in the histogram's height and direction, are commonly observed to evaluate momentum shifts.

data.name: NinjaScriptIndicatorDescriptionMAEnvelopes
data.value: MA Envelopes (Moving Average Envelopes) plots upper and lower bands offset by a user-defined percentage above and below a moving average. The bands expand or contract proportionally with the average and remain equidistant from it. Price interaction with the envelopes is commonly observed to assess relative extension from the underlying average.

data.name: NinjaScriptIndicatorDescriptionMAMA
data.value: MAMA (Mesa Adaptive Moving Average) is an adaptive moving average that adjusts its smoothing based on price phase and cycle analysis. It plots MAMA (Default) and a companion line, FAMA (Following Adaptive Moving Average). MAMA is designed to respond quickly to price changes while reducing lag during slower market conditions.

data.name: NinjaScriptIndicatorDescriptionMAX
data.value: MAX (Maximum) returns the highest value of the selected input series over the specified Period. It updates each bar and reflects the rolling maximum within the lookback window. MAX is commonly used for range calculations and channel-based indicators.

data.name: NinjaScriptIndicatorDescriptionMFI
data.value: MFI (Money Flow Index) is a volume-weighted momentum oscillator that incorporates both price and volume over the selected Period. It fluctuates between 0 and 100, with higher readings reflecting stronger positive money flow and lower readings reflecting stronger negative money flow. Extreme readings are commonly associated with overbought or oversold conditions.

data.name: NinjaScriptIndicatorDescriptionMIN
data.value: MIN (Minimum) returns the lowest value of the selected input series over the specified Period. It updates each bar and reflects the rolling minimum within the lookback window. MIN is commonly used in range-based calculations and channel-style indicators.

data.name: NinjaScriptIndicatorDescriptionMomentum
data.value: Video Tutorial: www.youtube.com/watch?v=lnf5g_GnLLE&list=PL3-s3qsUnfLSgA63mRRrNJv3lX4flD1UH&index=3\n\nMomentum measures the rate of change in price over the selected Period by comparing the current price to the price a set number of bars ago. Positive values indicate price is higher than it was at the lookback point, while negative values indicate it is lower. The magnitude reflects the strength of the price change over that period.

data.name: NinjaScriptIndicatorDescriptionNBarsDown
data.value: N Bars Down evaluates whether price has closed lower for the specified number of consecutive bars. When the defined sequence is met, the indicator plots a value of 1 for that bar; otherwise, it plots 0. This output is intended for condition detection in analysis or strategy logic rather than visual pattern annotation.

data.name: NinjaScriptIndicatorDescriptionNBarsUp
data.value: N Bars Up evaluates whether price has closed higher for the specified number of consecutive bars. When the defined sequence is met, the indicator plots a value of 1 for that bar; otherwise, it plots 0. This output is intended for condition detection in analysis or strategy logic rather than visual pattern annotation.

data.name: NinjaScriptIndicatorDescriptionOBV
data.value: Video Tutorial: www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZORmQeOKyBs&list=PL3-s3qsUnfLSgA63mRRrNJv3lX4flD1UH&index=10\n\nOBV (On-Balance Volume) is a cumulative volume indicator that adds volume when price closes higher and subtracts volume when price closes lower. The resulting line reflects the net flow of volume over time. OBV is commonly compared to price movement to assess confirmation or divergence in buying and selling pressure.

data.name: NinjaScriptIndicatorDescriptionParabolicSAR
data.value: Video Tutorial: www.youtube.com/watch?v=I5hQfS33D24&list=PL3-s3qsUnfLSgA63mRRrNJv3lX4flD1UH&index=14\n\nParabolic SAR (Parabolic Stop and Reverse) plots trailing stop levels that move incrementally with price based on an acceleration factor. When price crosses the SAR value, the indicator reverses position and begins plotting on the opposite side of price. It is commonly used to visualize trend direction and trailing stop placement.

data.name: NinjaScriptIndicatorDescriptionPFE
data.value: PFE (Polarized Fractal Efficiency) measures how efficiently price has moved from one point to another over the selected Period. It compares the direct distance between two prices to the total path traveled, producing values that fluctuate above and below zero. Higher absolute readings indicate more directional movement, while values near zero reflect less efficient, more sideways movement.

data.name: NinjaScriptIndicatorDescriptionPPO
data.value: PPO (Percentage Price Oscillator) measures the percentage difference between a fast and slow EMA (Exponential Moving Average). It functions similarly to MACD but expresses the relationship as a percentage rather than a raw value. PPO fluctuates around zero, with positive readings indicating the fast EMA is above the slow EMA and negative readings indicating the opposite.

data.name: NinjaScriptIndicatorDescriptionPriceOscillator
data.value: Price Oscillator plots the difference between two moving averages of the selected input series. Positive values indicate the shorter-period average is above the longer-period average, while negative values indicate it is below. The oscillator reflects shifts in relative momentum between the two averages.

data.name: NinjaScriptIndicatorDescriptionPriorDayOHLC
data.value: Prior Day OHLC (Prior Day Open/High/Low/Close) plots the previous session's Open, High, Low, and Close levels on the current chart. These values remain fixed throughout the active session and provide reference points based on prior session price data.

data.name: NinjaScriptIndicatorDescriptionRange
data.value: Range plots the difference between the High and Low of each bar. The value reflects the total price movement within the bar, without regard to direction. Larger readings indicate wider price movement during the bar, while smaller readings reflect tighter price activity.

data.name: NinjaScriptIndicatorDescriptionRegressionChannel
data.value: RegressionChannel plots a linear regression line over the selected Period along with upper and lower channel lines based on standard deviation. The central line represents the best-fit trend, while the outer bands reflect typical variation around that trend. The channel expands and contracts with volatility within the regression window.

data.name: NinjaScriptIndicatorDescriptionRIND
data.value: RIND (Relative Strength Index of Advancing/Declining Issues) is a market breadth indicator derived from advancing and declining issues. It applies an RSI-style calculation to breadth data rather than price, producing an oscillator that reflects the balance of advancing versus declining participation. Rising values indicate strengthening breadth, while falling values indicate weakening breadth.

data.name: NinjaScriptIndicatorDescriptionROC
data.value: ROC (Rate of Change) measures the percentage change in price over the selected Period. Positive values indicate price is higher than it was at the lookback point, while negative values indicate it is lower. The magnitude reflects the speed of price change over that interval.

data.name: NinjaScriptIndicatorDescriptionRSI
data.value: Video Tutorial: www.youtube.com/watch?v=KKSC3ikwRHY&list=PL3-s3qsUnfLSgA63mRRrNJv3lX4flD1UH&index=11\n\nRSI (Relative Strength Index) is a 0–100 momentum oscillator that compares the magnitude of recent gains to recent losses over the selected Period. Higher readings reflect stronger recent upward momentum, while lower readings reflect stronger recent downward momentum. The upper reference line is commonly associated with overbought conditions, and the lower reference line with oversold conditions. The indicator also plots Avg, a smoothed version of RSI based on the Smooth setting.

data.name: NinjaScriptIndicatorDescriptionRSquared
data.value: R Squared measures how closely price movement fits a linear regression line over the selected Period. Values range from 0 to 1, with higher readings indicating price is moving in a more consistent, trend-like manner, and lower readings indicating more random or non-trending behavior. It reflects trend quality rather than direction.

data.name: NinjaScriptIndicatorDescriptionRSS
data.value: RSS (Relative Spread Strength) measures the relative performance (spread) between two input series or instruments over the selected Period. The indicator reflects how one series is performing compared to the other, with rising values indicating strengthening relative performance and falling values indicating weakening relative performance. RSS is commonly used for comparative or pair analysis.

data.name: NinjaScriptIndicatorDescriptionRVI
data.value: RVI (Relative Vigor Index) compares the relationship between closing price and trading range over the selected Period. It plots the RVI along with a Signal line for comparison. Values fluctuate around zero, with positive readings reflecting stronger upward price bias and negative readings reflecting stronger downward bias. Crossovers between the RVI and its signal line are commonly observed for momentum shifts.

data.name: NinjaScriptIndicatorDescriptionSMA
data.value: Video Tutorial: www.youtube.com/watch?v=pcraBHC70B8&list=PL3-s3qsUnfLSgA63mRRrNJv3lX4flD1UH&index=19\n\nSMA (Simple Moving Average) calculates the arithmetic average of price over the selected Period. Each value in the lookback window is weighted equally. SMA is commonly used to smooth price data and assess general trend direction.

data.name: NinjaScriptIndicatorDescriptionStdDev
data.value: Std. Dev. (Standard Deviation) measures the dispersion of price values around their mean over the selected Period. Higher values indicate greater variability, while lower values reflect more stable price movement. Standard Deviation is often used as a volatility measure and as a component of other indicators.

data.name: NinjaScriptIndicatorDescriptionStdError
data.value: Std. Error (Standard Error) plots a Linear Regression line over the selected Period and two bands (Upper and Lower) offset by the calculated standard error of price around that regression line. Wider bands indicate price has deviated more from the regression fit, while narrower bands indicate price has stayed closer to the regression line.

data.name: NinjaScriptIndicatorDescriptionStochastics
data.value: Video Tutorial: www.youtube.com/watch?v=ES8UTUiHTaU&list=PL3-s3qsUnfLSgA63mRRrNJv3lX4flD1UH&index=4\n\nStochastics (Stochastics Oscillator) plots a smoothed %K and %D to measure the position of the close relative to the recent high-low range over the selected Period. The %K line is smoothed by the Smooth parameter, and %D is a moving average of %K. Values fluctuate between 0 and 100, with higher readings indicating price is closing near the top of its recent range and lower readings indicating it is closing near the bottom. Upper and lower reference lines are commonly associated with overbought and oversold conditions.

data.name: NinjaScriptIndicatorDescriptionStochasticsFast
data.value: Video Tutorial: www.youtube.com/watch?v=ES8UTUiHTaU&list=PL3-s3qsUnfLSgA63mRRrNJv3lX4flD1UH&index=4\n\nStochastics Fast plots the unsmoothed %K along with %D, a moving average of %K. Because %K is not internally smoothed, Fast Stochastics responds more quickly to price changes than the standard Stochastics indicator. Values range between 0 and 100 and reflect where the close sits within the recent high-low range. Upper and lower reference lines are commonly associated with overbought and oversold conditions.

data.name: NinjaScriptIndicatorDescriptionStochRSI
data.value: Video Tutorial: www.youtube.com/watch?v=ES8UTUiHTaU&list=PL3-s3qsUnfLSgA63mRRrNJv3lX4flD1UH&index=4\n\nStoch RSI (Stochastic RSI) applies the stochastic calculation to RSI (Relative Strength Index) values rather than directly to price. This creates an oscillator that measures the position of RSI within its own recent range. The result fluctuates between 0 and 1 and is designed to highlight momentum shifts within RSI itself.

data.name: NinjaScriptIndicatorDescriptionSUM
data.value: SUM returns the cumulative sum of the selected input series over the specified Period. It updates each bar and reflects the rolling total within the lookback window. SUM is commonly used as a building block in custom calculations or strategy development.

data.name: NinjaScriptIndicatorDescriptionSwing
data.value: Video Tutorial: www.youtube.com/watch?v=DlfyyIi-60M&list=PL3-s3qsUnfLSgA63mRRrNJv3lX4flD1UH&index=15\n\nSwing (Swing High/Low) identifies and plots swing highs and swing lows based on a specified Strength setting. A swing high forms when a bar's high is greater than surrounding bars, and a swing low forms when a bar's low is lower than surrounding bars. The indicator updates once the required number of confirming bars has completed and is commonly used to visualize structural turning points.

data.name: NinjaScriptIndicatorDescriptionT3
data.value: T3 (T3 Moving Average) is a multi-stage smoothed moving average designed to reduce lag while maintaining smoothness. It applies a series of exponential smoothing calculations with a volume factor to control responsiveness. T3 is commonly used to track trend direction with less noise than traditional moving averages.

data.name: NinjaScriptIndicatorDescriptionTEMA
data.value: TEMA (Triple Exponential Moving Average) reduces lag by combining multiple exponential moving average calculations into a single value. Compared to a standard EMA, TEMA responds more quickly to price changes while still smoothing short-term fluctuations. It is often used to identify trend direction with increased responsiveness.

data.name: NinjaScriptIndicatorDescriptionTMA
data.value: TMA (Triangular Moving Average) is a double-smoothed moving average that applies a smoothing calculation twice, resulting in a very smooth line. Because of this additional smoothing, TMA reacts more slowly to price changes than SMA or EMA and is commonly used to highlight longer-term trend structure.

data.name: NinjaScriptIndicatorDescriptionTRIX
data.value: TRIX (Triple Exponential Average Oscillator) measures the rate of change of a triple-smoothed exponential moving average. It fluctuates around zero, with positive values indicating upward momentum in the smoothed average and negative values indicating downward momentum. Because of the triple smoothing, TRIX filters shorter-term noise and emphasizes broader momentum shifts.

data.name: NinjaScriptIndicatorDescriptionTSF
data.value: TSF (Time Series Forecast) plots the projected value of a linear regression line at the current bar based on the selected Period. Unlike a standard regression line, TSF extends the regression calculation forward to estimate the expected value at the end of the lookback window. It is commonly used to visualize trend direction and projected continuation based on regression analysis.

data.name: NinjaScriptIndicatorDescriptionTSI
data.value: TSI (True Strength Index) is a double-smoothed momentum oscillator that measures price change relative to its recent volatility. It fluctuates above and below zero, with positive readings reflecting stronger upward momentum and negative readings reflecting stronger downward momentum. A signal line is typically plotted for crossover comparison.

data.name: NinjaScriptIndicatorDescriptionUltimateOscillator
data.value: Ultimate Oscillator combines momentum calculations across three different lookback periods into a single bounded oscillator. Values range between 0 and 100 and reflect buying pressure relative to true range over multiple timeframes. It is designed to reduce the impact of relying on a single period and to provide a broader view of momentum conditions.

data.name: NinjaScriptIndicatorDescriptionVMA
data.value: VMA (Variable Moving Average, VIDYA – Variable Index Dynamic Average) is an adaptive moving average that adjusts its smoothing factor based on market conditions. It becomes more responsive during stronger directional movement and smoother during quieter conditions. VMA is designed to balance responsiveness and noise reduction.

data.name: NinjaScriptIndicatorDescriptionVOL
data.value: VOL (Volume) plots the total traded volume for each bar. The value reflects the number of contracts, shares, or units traded during the bar's interval. Volume is commonly used to assess participation and compare activity levels across bars.

data.name: NinjaScriptIndicatorDescriptionVOLMA
data.value: VOLMA (Volume Moving Average) plots a moving average of Volume (VOL) over the selected Period. It smooths volume data to help identify relative increases or decreases in trading activity compared to its recent average.

data.name: NinjaScriptIndicatorDescriptionVolumeOscillator
data.value: Volume Oscillator measures the difference between a short-term and long-term moving average of volume. Positive values indicate the shorter average is above the longer average, reflecting relatively increasing activity, while negative values indicate relatively decreasing activity.

data.name: NinjaScriptIndicatorDescriptionVROC
data.value: VROC (Volume Rate of Change) measures the percentage change in volume over the selected Period. Positive values indicate volume has increased relative to the lookback point, while negative values indicate it has decreased. The magnitude reflects how quickly participation levels are changing.

data.name: NinjaScriptIndicatorDescriptionVWMA
data.value: VWMA (Volume Weighted Moving Average) calculates a moving average that weights each price by its corresponding volume over the selected Period. Periods with higher volume have greater influence on the average. VWMA is commonly used to reflect price movement adjusted for trading activity.

data.name: NinjaScriptIndicatorDescriptionWilliamsR
data.value: Williams R (Williams %R) is a momentum oscillator that measures the position of the current close relative to the highest high and lowest low over the selected Period. Values fluctuate between -100 and 0, with readings near 0 indicating price is closing near the top of its recent range and readings near -100 indicating it is closing near the bottom. Extreme readings are commonly associated with overbought or oversold conditions.

data.name: NinjaScriptIndicatorDescriptionWMA
data.value: WMA (Weighted Moving Average) calculates a moving average that assigns greater weight to more recent prices within the selected Period. This weighting makes WMA more responsive to current price changes compared to a simple moving average.

data.name: NinjaScriptIndicatorDescriptionZigZag
data.value: Zig Zag identifies and connects significant swing highs and swing lows based on a user-defined deviation value (such as percentage or points). It filters out smaller price movements to emphasize larger directional swings. Because it adjusts as new price data forms, historical swing points may update until confirmed.

data.name: NinjaScriptIndicatorDescriptionZLEMA
data.value: ZLEMA (Zero Lag Exponential Moving Average) is a modified exponential moving average designed to reduce lag by compensating for the delay inherent in traditional EMA calculations. It aims to track price more closely while maintaining smoothing characteristics.

data.name: NinjaScriptIndicatorDescriptionBarTimer
data.value: Bar Timer displays the remaining time for the currently forming time-based bar. The countdown updates in real time and resets when a new bar begins. This indicator is intended for time-based bar types and helps monitor bar completion without affecting price calculations.

data.name: NinjaScriptIndicatorDescriptionBuySellVolume
data.value: Buy Sell Volume separates total volume into estimated buying volume and selling volume based on trade direction or price movement within the bar. This helps illustrate whether activity is dominated by buyers or sellers during a given period. The indicator focuses on participation imbalance rather than price alone and is often used to assess momentum behind price moves.\n\nThis indicator relies on intrabar order flow data and will only display historically when Tick Replay is enabled; otherwise, it plots in real-time only.

data.name: NinjaScriptIndicatorDescriptionCandlestickPattern
data.value: Video Tutorial: www.youtube.com/watch?v=ydDRqD99byE&list=PL3-s3qsUnfLSgA63mRRrNJv3lX4flD1UH&index=5\n\nCandlestick Pattern detects a wide range of predefined candlestick formations based on the Select pattern setting. Only the user-selected pattern is evaluated. When the specified formation is confirmed, the indicator places text on the chart at the occurrence and colors the related bar(s) to visually highlight the pattern. It is designed to identify and emphasize recognized price formations.

data.name: NinjaScriptIndicatorDescriptionSampleCustomRender
data.value: Sample Custom Render is an example NinjaTrader indicator that demonstrates custom SharpDX rendering techniques (e.g., drawing your own visuals directly on the chart). It’s designed for education and development, use it as a reference for building, testing, and extending custom rendering workflows. * Purpose: Show how to implement custom SharpDX rendering in an indicator * What it is not: Not an analytical indicator and does not generate trading signals * Best for: Developers learning rendering patterns, performance considerations, and chart-drawing structure For more background on NinjaTrader and building custom tools, visit: https://ninjatrader.com/ Tip: Try pairing this example with your own colors, shapes, and update logic to explore rendering behavior under different chart conditions.

data.name: NinjaScriptIndicatorDescriptionDarvas
data.value: Darvas (Darvas Box) plots dynamic upper and lower price levels based on recent highs and lows to form "boxes" around consolidating price action. When price establishes a new high or low outside the prior box, the levels adjust to reflect the updated range. This indicator is commonly used to visualize breakout zones and structured price ranges.

data.name: NinjaScriptIndicatorDescriptionPivots
data.value: Video Tutorial: www.youtube.com/watch?v=ATddfGiV6SY&list=PL3-s3qsUnfLSgA63mRRrNJv3lX4flD1UH&index=13\n\nPivots (Pivot Points) plots standard floor-trader pivot levels calculated from a prior period's high, low, and close. The indicator displays a central pivot along with projected support and resistance levels that update each new session or selected timeframe. These levels are commonly used as structured reference points for price movement.

data.name: NinjaScriptIndicatorDescriptionRangeCounter
data.value: Range Counter displays the remaining price range needed to complete the currently forming range bar. The value updates in real time as the bar expands and resets when a new bar begins. This indicator is intended for range-based bar types and helps monitor bar completion without affecting price calculations.

data.name: NinjaScriptIndicatorDescriptionTickCounter
data.value: Tick Counter displays the remaining number of ticks needed to complete the currently forming tick bar. The count updates in real time as new ticks arrive and resets when a new bar begins. This indicator is intended for tick-based bar types and helps monitor bar completion without affecting price calculations.

data.name: NinjaScriptIndicatorDescriptionVolumeCounter
data.value: Volume Counter accumulates and displays the total volume traded within the current bar, updating in real time as new trades occur. The count resets when a new bar begins. This indicator is informational and focuses on intrabar volume tracking.

data.name: NinjaScriptIndicatorDescriptionVolumeProfile
data.value: Volume Profile displays the distribution of traded volume at specific price levels over a selected range. It highlights areas of higher and lower participation, often identifying high-volume nodes and low-volume areas. Volume Profile is commonly used to visualize price levels where trading activity has been concentrated.\n\nThis indicator relies on intrabar order flow data and will only display historically when Tick Replay is enabled; otherwise, it plots in real-time only.

data.name: NinjaScriptIndicatorDescriptionVolumeZones
data.value: Volume Zones draws a horizontal volume histogram using only the bars currently visible on the chart. The visible price range is divided into the number of slices defined by the BarCount property, and volume is aggregated within each slice.\n\nFor each slice, volume is separated into up volume (bars where Close > Open) and down volume (bars where Close ? Open), and the histogram is colored accordingly. This provides a visual reference of where trading activity has concentrated within the current chart view, rather than over a fixed historical period.

data.name: NinjaScriptIndicatorDescriptionVolumeUpDown
data.value: Volume Up Down separates total volume into up volume and down volume based on whether price closed higher or lower than the previous bar. This helps visualize buying versus selling activity within each period and compare relative participation on advancing versus declining bars.

data.name: NinjaScriptIndicatorDescriptionMovingAverageRibbon
data.value: Moving Average Ribbon plots multiple moving averages of increasing lengths on the same panel to visualize trend structure. When the averages are aligned and spaced apart, it suggests stronger directional movement; when they compress or cross frequently, it reflects consolidation. The ribbon provides a layered view of short-, medium-, and longer-term averages.

data.name: NinjaScriptIndicatorDescriptionNetChangeDisplay
data.value: Net Change Display displays the net price change for the current session relative to the prior session's close. It presents the change as a value and/or percentage directly on the chart. This indicator is informational and does not calculate momentum or trend signals.

data.name: NinjaScriptIndicatorDescriptionPriceLine
data.value: PriceLine (Price Line) displays real-time horizontal reference lines for the current Ask, Bid, and/or Last price directly on the chart. Each line can be enabled/disabled independently to keep key live pricing levels visible.

data.name: NinjaScriptIndicatorDescriptionDisparityIndex
data.value: Disparity Index measures the percentage difference between the current price and moving average over the chosen Period. Positive values indicate price is trading above the average, while negative values indicate it is below. Larger deviations reflect greater separation from the average, helping visualize relative extension from typical price levels.

data.name: NinjaScriptIndicatorDescriptionMoneyFlowOscillator
data.value: Money Flow Oscillator measures buying and selling pressure by comparing positive and negative money flow over the selected Period. It incorporates both price movement and volume to produce an oscillator that fluctuates around a central line. Positive values reflect stronger buying pressure, while negative values reflect stronger selling pressure.

data.name: NinjaScriptIndicatorDescriptionMcClellanOscillator
data.value: McClellan Oscillator is a breadth indicator calculated from the difference between two exponential averages of advancing and declining issues. It fluctuates above and below zero, reflecting shifts in overall market participation strength. Rising values indicate improving breadth, while falling values indicate weakening breadth.\n\nThis indicator require ADV and DECL index data

data.name: NinjaScriptIndicatorDescriptionVortex
data.value: Vortex plots two lines, VI+ and VI-, derived from upward and downward price movement over the selected Period. When VI+ is above VI-, upward directional movement is stronger; when VI- is above VI+, downward movement is stronger. The separation between the lines reflects the strength of directional movement.

data.name: NinjaScriptIndicatorDescriptionPsychologicalLine
data.value: PSY (Psychological Line) measures the percentage of bars that closed higher than the previous bar over the selected Period. Values range from 0 to 100, with higher readings indicating a greater proportion of up-closing bars and lower readings indicating more down-closing bars. It reflects short-term market sentiment based on closing direction frequency.

data.name: NinjaScriptIndicatorDescriptionChoppinessIndex
data.value: Choppiness Index quantifies whether the market is trending or moving sideways over the selected Period. Higher values suggest choppier, range-bound conditions, while lower values indicate stronger directional movement. It is commonly used to assess overall market structure rather than predict direction.

data.name: NinjaScriptIndicatorDescriptionBlockVolume
data.value: Block Volume identifies and marks individual trades whose size meets or exceeds the specified volume threshold. Each qualifying trade is highlighted on the chart to make large transactions easier to spot. This indicator requires historical tick data to accurately detect and display block trades, as it evaluates individual executions rather than aggregated bar volume. It focuses on trade size and participation, not price direction.

data.name: NinjaScriptIndicatorDescriptionCamarillaPivots
data.value: Camarilla Pivots plots a series of intraday support and resistance levels calculated from the prior session's high, low, and close. These levels are labeled R and S levels and are commonly used to frame potential reaction zones within the current session. The indicator automatically updates each session and is designed for session-based analysis rather than long-term trend evaluation.

data.name: NinjaScriptIndicatorDescriptionFibonacciPivots
data.value: Fibonacci Pivots plots session-based support and resistance levels derived from the prior period's high, low, and close using Fibonacci ratios. Levels are projected above and below a central pivot and update automatically at the start of each new session. These levels are commonly used as structured reference points for intraday price movement.

data.name: NinjaScriptIndicatorDescriptionTrendLines
data.value: Video Tutorial: www.youtube.com/watch?v=kOXxE6r5IE0&list=PL3-s3qsUnfLSgA63mRRrNJv3lX4flD1UH&index=7\n\nTrend Lines automatically detects and draws trend lines based on recent swing highs and swing lows. Lines update as new qualifying swing points form, helping visualize directional structure and potential areas of support or resistance. This indicator focuses on structural price relationships rather than momentum calculations.

Positive readings suggest the instruments tend to move in the same direction, negative readings suggest they move inversely, and values near zero indicate little consistent relationship.

data.name: NinjaScriptIndicatorDescriptionCOT
data.value: Video Tutorial: www.youtube.com/watch?v=PorVWVVRs6s&list=PL3-s3qsUnfLSgA63mRRrNJv3lX4flD1UH&index=2\n\nCOT (Commitment of Traders) displays positioning data from the CFTC's weekly Commitment of Traders report, broken down by trader categories. The report is released each Friday and reflects positions as of the prior Tuesday. The indicator plots selected COT values to visualize changes in market participation over time. It is based on published report data (not real-time transactions) and is best viewed on a weekly chart. To receive the latest data, "Download COTR data at startup" must be enabled in Settings.

data.name: FVGDescription
data.value: FVG (Fair Value Gap) examines three consecutive bars to identify and highlight a price gap between the high/low of the first and third bars. When the ranges of the first and third bars do not overlap, the resulting gap is drawn on the chart and can optionally extend forward. FVG regions are commonly observed as areas where price may revisit. The indicator supports filtering by minimum gap size and limiting the number of displayed gaps.

data.name: NinjaScriptIndicatorDescriptionBollingerBandWidth
data.value: Bollinger Band Width measures Bollinger Band width as a percentage of the moving average, reflecting how wide the bands are relative to price level. Higher values indicate expanding volatility and lower values indicate contracting volatility.

data.name: NinjaScriptIndicatorDescriptionPercentB
data.value: %B (Percent B) measures where the current price is positioned within the Bollinger (Bollinger Bands) range. Values near 0 indicate price is near the lower band, values near 1 indicate price is near the upper band, and values outside 0–1 indicate price is below the lower band or above the upper band.

data.name: NinjaScriptIndicatorDescriptionPerformance
data.value: Performance (PERF) shows the percent change of the current value relative to the first value in the loaded series. It is calculated as ((current − first) / first) × 100 and updates as the chart’s loaded history changes.

data.name: NinjaScriptIndicatorDescriptionPriceVolumeTrend
data.value: PVT (Price Volume Trend) is a cumulative volume-based indicator that adds or subtracts volume based on the percent change in close from the prior bar. The line rises when up moves occur on higher relative volume and falls when down moves occur on higher relative volume, providing a running view of price change weighted by volume.

data.name: NinjaScriptIndicatorDescriptionMassIndex
data.value: MI (Mass Index) measures range expansion by applying a double EMA to the bar range (High − Low) and summing the ratio of the single EMA to the double EMA over the specified lookback. Rising values indicate persistent range expansion, while falling values indicate range contraction.

data.name: NinjaScriptIndicatorDescriptionForceIndex
data.value: FI (Force Index) combines price change and volume by calculating (Close − prior Close) × Volume, then smoothing it with an EMA. Positive values reflect stronger upward pressure with volume participation, while negative values reflect stronger downward pressure with volume participation.

data.name: NinjaScriptIndicatorDescriptionDetrendedPriceOscillator
data.value: DPO (Detrended Price Oscillator) removes longer-term trend influence by comparing a past price value to a shifted simple moving average. The result oscillates around zero and is used to highlight shorter-term cycles and swings without the longer-term trend component.
